# DB2 Auto-generated Key Backfill

DB2 supports identity columns and sequences. For identity columns, JDBC generated keys can be used; for sequences, getting the value before INSERT is more recommended.

IBM documentation states that DB2 JDBC supports reading auto-generated keys, but batch generated keys have limitations — under certain configurations, a `PreparedStatement` prepared to return generated keys cannot be used for batch updates. See [IBM DB2 generated keys documentation](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/db2-for-zos/12.0.0?topic=sql-retrieval-automatically-generated-keys-in-jdbc-applications).

dbVisitor therefore adopts a conservative strategy under DB2: regular JDBC batch when no backfill columns; row-by-row execution when backfill columns exist, to avoid uncertainties from batch backfill ordering and driver limitations.

## IDENTITY Column

```sql
CREATE TABLE user_info (
    id   BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(64),
    age  INT
)
```

## Lambda / BaseMapper

```java title='DB2 IDENTITY mapping'
@Table("user_info")
public class UserInfo {
    @Column(value = "id", primary = true, keyType = KeyType.Auto)
    private Long id;

    @Column("name")
    private String name;
}
```

```java title='Read backfilled primary key after Lambda insert'
UserInfo user = new UserInfo();
user.setName("mali");

LambdaTemplate lambda = ...
lambda.insert(UserInfo.class)
      .applyEntity(user)
      .executeSumResult();

Long id = user.getId();
```

## Mapper XML

```xml title='DB2 generated keys'
<insert id="insertUser"
        useGeneratedKeys="true"
        keyProperty="id"
        keyColumn="id">
    INSERT INTO user_info (name)
    VALUES (#{name})
</insert>
```

## Annotation Mapper

```java
@Insert(
    value = "INSERT INTO user_info (name) VALUES (#{name})",
    useGeneratedKeys = true,
    keyProperty = "id",
    keyColumn = "id"
)
int insertUser(UserInfo user);
```

## Sequence

DB2 dialect supports reading sequences:

```sql
VALUES NEXT VALUE FOR user_info_seq
```

Mapper XML:

```xml
<insert id="insertUser">
    <selectKey keyProperty="id" keyColumn="id" order="BEFORE">
        VALUES NEXT VALUE FOR user_info_seq
    </selectKey>
    INSERT INTO user_info (id, name)
    VALUES (#{id}, #{name})
</insert>
```

Lambda / BaseMapper:

```java
@KeySeq("user_info_seq")
@Column(value = "id", primary = true, keyType = KeyType.Sequence)
private Long id;
```

## Dialect Strategy

DB2's current strategy is as follows:

| Scenario | GeneratedKeyStrategy |
| --- | --- |
| No backfill columns | `JdbcBatch` |
| `Into` + with backfill columns | `OneByOne` |
| `Ignore` + with backfill columns | `OneByOne` |
| `Update` + with backfill columns | `OneByOne` |

`DuplicateKeyStrategy.Ignore` / `Update` are implemented via DB2 `MERGE`, requiring primary key columns.

## Design Principles

- identity: use `KeyType.Auto` or `useGeneratedKeys=true`.
- sequence: use `selectKey` / `@SelectKeySql` / `KeyType.Sequence` to get value before INSERT.
- DB2 uses conservative row-by-row execution when generated keys backfill is needed; regular JDBC batch can be used when no backfill is required.
- General documentation: see [Generated Keys](../../guides/core/mapper/annotation_insert#generated-keys).
